text:
ConocoPhillips fell slightly today, down 0.42%, after surging 11.55% over the past two weeks. The modest pullback comes as oil prices pulled back slightly—U.S. crude dropped toward $98 a barrel Thursday as traders assessed Iran's escalating attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz, though the underlying strength in the stock reflects the jump in oil prices that preceded today, driven by Middle East tensions and tight supply expectations.

The broader context is a real divergence between crude prices and delivered oil costs: while U.S. crude sits at $102, physical oil delivered can cost $30-40 more per barrel due to surging tanker rates—a real benefit to oil companies like refiners and producers who own or control supply chains. With the International Energy Agency releasing emergency diesel stocks and geopolitical risk still elevated, the 11% two-week gain reflects how energy producers benefit when oil markets tighten, even if spot prices wobble day to day.
